Rukmiṇī
------------------------------------------
Whenever God विष्णु incarnated himself on this earth, his consort लक्ष्मी too would do so as his spouse. In his इन्चर्नतिओन् as कृष्ण, लक्ष्मी came down as रुक्मिणी.
Rukmiṇī was the daughter of Bhīṣmaka, the king of Vidarbha. Though she wanted to marry कृष्ण only, her elder brother Rukmi was opposing it vehemently. So she sent a secret message through a trusted ब्राह्मण to कृष्ण, who successfully managed to abduct her and later marry her.
Pradyumna was her son and Cārumatī, her daughter.
She immolated herself in a fire after the demise of कृष्ण.

Rukmāṅgada
------------------------------------------
Great devotees of God have often been subjected to severe tests. But, by the very grace of God Himself, they have also come out successful. king रुक्माङ्गद is one such glorious example.
An ardent devotee of विष्णु, the king रुक्माङ्गद was fastidious in the observance of एकादशी (eleventh day after full-मोओन् or new-मोओन्) as a vrata (religious vow) consisting of total ड़स्तिन्ग् and worship of God विष्णु.
Once, as ill-luck would have it, he fell in love with a beautiful woman, मोहिनी by name, promising her to do whatever she wanted.
On an एकादशी day when Rukmāṅ-gada was ड़स्तिन्ग्, she demanded that either he should break his fast or kill his son Dharmāṅgada (son of the chief queen Sandhyāvalī). रुक्माङ्गद was not willing to do the first and was hesitant to do the second, when his son voluntarily offered to sacrifice himself. Just as he was about to behead his son, विष्णु appeared on the scene and took away the whole family to वैकुण्ठ, his celestial abode.
Mohinī had been specially sent by ब्रह्मा, the creator, to subject the king रुक्माङ्गद to this test.
The एकादशी day on which this happened is observed even today as वैकुण्ठ एकादशी (eleventh day of the bright fortnight in the month of Mārgaśira, usually in December).
